thread:
Maria: Proposal — introduce an ownership-splitter stage between ingest and the canonical ledger. splitter emits provisional_attribution events that separately count prefix-cache hits and model-gen tokens. goal: keep generation fast (no blocking writes to main ledger) while producing small, auditable deltas for later consolidation.
Alex: sounds useful. main question: how do we avoid double-charging when retries/happy-path fallbacks happen?
Maria: plan: events are deterministic keyed by (request_id, generation_id, fingerprint). splitter emits a provisional idempotent delta and a compact proof-frame reference. finalizer will consolidate by generation_id once we see a stable commit signal.
Shiv: deterministic keys help, but we still need a way to expire provisional claims if the finalizer never shows up (network partition, crash). TTLs? tombstones?
Maria: TTL on provisional_attribution + a reconciliation job that treats missing finalizers as "orphaned_provisional" and routes to a repair queue. TTL short-ish (5m) to avoid long-lived partial credits.
Jordan: repair queue is fine, but audits will want a complete trail. The proof-frame should include a small fingerprint of the model checkpoint, prompt hash, and shard metadata so an auditor can replay.
Priya: what about interactive chat where prefix-cache is frequently used? splitting per-token could be noisy. Maybe we emit aggregated provisional deltas per-request chunk (e.g., per-100 tokens) to reduce noise and event volume.
Alex: agree on aggregation. also we should keep the provisional events small so the generation path can emit them synchronously (<=1 extra IO). that suggests using a local write-ahead buffer that flushes to the splitter asynchronously.
Shiv: tradeoffs: a local buffer reduces latency but increases risk of lost provisional events on host crash. If we buffer and crash, finalizer will never see the provisional and core ledger might still get full event later — must handle reconciliation idempotently.
Maria: recon semantics: provisional events are append-only with a provenance fingerprint; finalizer does an atomic compare-and-merge into the ledger using generation_id. If the ledger already has matching tokens, we mark the provisional as reconciled and noop.
Priya: how does billing compute SLOs that rely on real-time credit consumption (for quota enforcement)? They need near-real-time visibility of provisional deltas. We can stream provisional aggregates into the quota service with a "provisional" flag and have soft quotas that only block on final ledger entries.
Jordan: audits want immutable traces. Where do we store proof-frames? Keep them in the audit store (cold) and reference them from the provisional event. proof-frames are small (json with prompt hash, model, seq metadata).
Alex: infrastructure: Kafka topic "splitter.provisional" (compact key by generation_id) then finalizer reads, writes to canonical topic "billing.ledger". repair job monitors watermark and orphan TTLs.
Shiv: another worry: multi-tenant fairness when we aggregate provisional deltas. If one tenant sends many small requests, batching could delay their visible charge and affect chargeback reporting. We need tenant-aware flush thresholds.
Maria: yes, tenant-aware heuristics: flush on either token count threshold OR time threshold OR memory pressure. Defaults: 100 tokens or 3s, whichever first.
Priya: can we surface a debug endpoint to fetch the provisional stream for a request_id so SEs can debug discrepancies?
Alex: yes, expose read-only view with proof-frame links, but restricted to internal roles.
billing-bot: deploy status: prototype splitter service (canary) deployed to staging. metrics: provisional-events/sec = 420, avg emit latency = 6ms.
Maria: next steps: doc RFC draft with sequence diagram + failure modes, prototype metrics to capture (emit latency, reconciliation lag, orphan rate), and an SLO for reconciliation (e.g., 99.9% reconciled within 2m).
Jordan: +1 to the RFC. add examples for function-calling/streaming where partial KV-cache hits change attribution mid-generation.
Shiv: I'll draft the failure-mode section (crash, partition, duplicate generation_id) and run it by infra.
Priya: I'll prototype the tenant-aware flush heuristics and simulate a bursty tenant pattern.
Maria: thanks — marking action items: Shiv (failure modes), Priya (flush heuristics), Alex (sequence diagram + infra topics), Jordan (audit proof-frame format). I'll open RFC in docs and ping team for review. :thumbsup:
